clue.text: Brightly coloured as a fish?

definitions.meaning: loud and showy in colour, gaudy
read as ..., like a gar, the long-snouted freshwater fish, with -ish meaning resembling

explanation.surface: A question whether something is as vividly coloured as a tropical fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a gar is a fish and the suffix -ish means 'like', so 'as a fish' is gar-ish; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something gaudy, loud and over-bright in colour is described as this.

clue.text: Soldier's blanket made up of appropriate fabric predominantly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a rug is a blanket

indicators.note: most of the fabric word is kept, losing its tail

parts.note: khaki cloth is fitting for a soldier's uniform

explanation.surface: A soldier's blanket woven mostly of the right cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' turns RUG upwards to GUR; 'predominantly' keeps KHA of KHAKI. The 's links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Nepalese soldier serving in the British or Indian army.

clue.text: Record-keeper rigs Libor's closing rate corruptly

indicators.note: the letters are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the closing letter of Libor, R, followed by the word rate as written

explanation.surface: An official fixes the Libor closing rate dishonestly, recalling the 2012 interest-rate scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Libor is the London interbank lending rate whose rigging was a banking scandal. 'closing' takes only the last letter of Libor, which joins the other words in the pool that 'corruptly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who keeps registers of births, marriages and deaths keeps records.

clue.text: Last five runs of the season

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Cross erected for deity

clue.text: Compete with son's opinions

clue.text: Rule's a setback for German golfer

clue.text: Smack is served using this

clue.text: Soldiers can't enter this tricky swamp — one went first, as an example, being swallowed up
